clinicalPearls: A self-limiting syndrome of joint pain with MRI bone marrow oedema and no identifiable structural cause
It is an umbrella that includes transient osteoporosis of the hip and regional migratory osteoporosis
It typically affects weight-bearing joints of the lower limb and can migrate between sites over time
MRI shows marrow oedema without the subchondral necrosis of avascular necrosis or a fracture line
The main differentials are early avascular necrosis, subchondral insufficiency fracture and infection
It resolves spontaneously over months, and management is supportive with protected weight bearing and analgesia
reference.pathophysiology: Bone marrow oedema syndrome denotes reversible accumulation of interstitial fluid within bone marrow producing pain and characteristic MRI signal change, without an underlying tumour, infection, established osteonecrosis or fracture. The mechanism is uncertain and probably multifactorial, involving transient alterations in local perfusion, increased intraosseous pressure and a reparative or neurovascular response. Its migratory and self-limiting nature and the absence of necrosis distinguish it from avascular necrosis, though the two may overlap on a spectrum.
additionalInvestigations: MRI demonstrating marrow oedema without necrosis or fracture
Radiographs and, where needed, follow-up imaging
Assessment of osteoporosis risk and secondary causes
Exclusion of malignancy where features are atypical
redFlags: Imaging evidence of osteonecrosis with impending collapse
reference.prognosis: The syndrome is benign and self-limiting, generally resolving over several months, though symptoms may migrate to other joints before settling.
pitfalls: Confusing it with avascular necrosis and over-treating
Missing a subchondral insufficiency fracture or malignancy
Not protecting the affected weight-bearing bone
management: Supportive care with protected weight bearing and analgesia while the syndrome resolves spontaneously over months
Bisphosphonates or a prostacyclin analogue such as iloprost to accelerate resolution of pain and marrow oedema in more severe or persistent cases
Physiotherapy to maintain joint range of movement and muscle strength
Assess and treat osteoporosis and secondary causes of bone marrow oedema
Follow-up MRI to confirm resolution and exclude progression to avascular necrosis or a subchondral insufficiency fracture
Core decompression considered for refractory hip disease
